For the sake of convenience the parties shall be denoted as IP Gaon Sabha i.e. in reference to Gaon Sabha and IP1 and IP2 as the individual claimants.
2. Notice of the reference petition was directed upon the interested parties.
All of them have filed their respective claim petitions.
They have also duly replied to the claim petition of the opposite party.
3. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 22.08.2016 following issues were settled by my Ld.
Predecessor:
(1)Which of the IPs is entitled to the compensation with regard to the land under reference?

Village Tajpur Khurd, New Delhi for the years 200304, 200405, 200506, 200607, 200708 and 200809 as Ex.R1 to Ex.R6 and certified copies of Khatoni pertaining to the same land for the years 199596 and 200102 as Mark A (Colly).
5. On behalf of IP No.2 IP Col. VPS Dahiya tendered his evidence by way of an affidavit as Ex.IP2W1/A.

He had filed copies of title documents i.e. GPA and Agreement to Sell dated 07.05.1996 in respect of plot/land measuring 200 sq yards bearing plot no.L36, Comprising in Kh.
No.11/5(416) in the colony named as Defence Enclave situated within the revenue estate of village Tajpur, PO Chhawla, Najafgarh, New Delhi which were executed by previous owner Smt. Ex.IPW1/3 and Ex.IPW1/4 respectively and copy of order dated 12.12.2007 issued by Lt.

5.1 During his cross examination he deposed that he was not aware as to the fact whether Sukhdev Singh had obtained approval from competent Govt authority for developing a residential colony on agricultural land.

sentences.text: 3 12. Now the only point or issue which has been framed with regard to the apportionment of the compensation interse the parties.

12.1 For the sake of convenience the said issue is reproduced as under:
(1)Which of the IPs is entitled to the compensation with regard to the land under reference?
Onus on parties.

12.2 Relevant to note herein that proceedings U/s 81 of the DLR Act were initiated by Gaon Sabha Tajpur Khurd against Sushila Gupta w/o Chander Prakash which was disposed of and the claim of Gaon Sabha was allowed in terms of order dated 20.10.1999.
The said case file was numbered as 145/NG/97.
Order was passed by Ms. Varsha Joshi, RA/SDM.
It is also important to note that Sushila Gupta had participated in the said proceedings and she was represented by her lawyer.
The record of the proceedings has been filed by the IP 1 and IP 2 - qua the said aspect the evidence of Kuldeep IP2W5 has been led.

12.3 Now suffice to again note herein that this order was not challenged and incorporated in the Khatoni wherein it is endorsed that as per orders passed by Ms. Varsha Joshi, SDM, Najafgarh, the Khasra number 11/5 (416) stood vested in Gaon Sabha.

12.4 Now counsel for the IP1 and IP2 i.e. the individual claimants had argued that the claimants were not made aware about the vesting order and they were also not parties to the said proceedings which in a manner were taken at their back.
According to them or as per their contention the vesting order does not infringe their rights insofar as the property in question is concerned.
12.5 In my considered opinion this is a fallacious plea.
First of all the proceedings were continued/pending for considerable period of time as the same commenced in the year 1997 and culminated in the year 1999.

As per the reading of the case file there was colonization on the said properties and to revert the land for the use of agricultural purposes would be a costly affair as Rs.2.5 lakh would be the cost for the same.
Subsequently in the order sheet dated 20.10.1999 it is also reflected that the area is ready for construction of a colony.

12.6 The case of IP1 and IP2 is also to the effect that they have purchased plots in Khasra no.11/5 and there was one organization by the name of Defence Housing Society to which they have made payments.
Certain receipts were also placed on record.

Infact in the application addressed to the Dy.
Commissioner, South West whereby Brigadier Sanjay Sharma IP2 sought information through RTI.
He also admitted that he had purchased a plot in Defence Housing Organization i.e. bearing No.L 38.
Further reading of the award reflects that VPS Dahihya had sought Rs.20 Lakhs as cost of construction.
The name of Brigadier Sanjay Sharma does not reflect in the name of the interested parties who had staked this claim.
However, subsequently he had also joined and later on a reference was sent incorporating his name as well.

12.7 The cumulative reading of the aforesaid makes it apparent that owing to plotting being done in agricultural land, proceedings were initiated U/s 81 of DLR Act whereby land in question was vested in Gaon Sabha in terms order passed by SDM which was not assailed by any of the parties including IP1 and IP2 or their predecessors in interest.

sentences.text: Since SDM/RA had acted in accordance with law as per the scheme of DLR Act, said proceedings cannot be ignored from the zone of consideration for the reason that IP1 and IP2 were not parties thereto.
Same to my mind is completely untenable plea.

13. Now if I look at the documents whereby parties have acquired property in question or raise their claim, it is important to note that the original owner of the property was Smt. Sushila Gupta and she in turn had executed documents i.e. GPA, Agreement to Sell & Purchase, Will, Affidavit etc in favour of Major Sukhdev Singh.

Subsequently Navjot Singh and Major Sukhdev Singh had executed registered GPA, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit and Will in favour of Vijay Pal Singh in respect of plot no.L36.
13.1
Now insofar as documents of Brigadier Sanjay Sharma are concerned same are also to the same effect i.e. registered GPA, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit etc. 13.2
Now fact of the matter is that neither Navjot Singh nor Major Sukhdev Singh had staked any claim for compensation.
Neither Sushila Gupta had lodged any claim for compensation.
They had disposed of the land by way of said documents whereby plotting was done.
By virtue of said documents, some of which are registered atleast prima facie the genuineness of the sale transactions between the parties can be inferred.
13.3 Coming to the crucial point for adjudication as to the apportionment of the compensation interse the competing parties.
Fact of the matter is that moment the land in question is vested in Gaon Sabha the original Bhumidar's rights or interest in the land ceases and those rights are vested in Gaon Sabha.
Obviously Bhumidari rights are creation of statute and the same can be enjoyed subject to the restriction imposed by the statute.
Owing to the infringement carried out by the individual Bhumidhar those rights are taken over or taken back and vested in Gaon Sabha.

13.4 As this Court has to determine the aspect of compensation interse parties, reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court passed in the case of Raj Singh & Anr v. Union of India &
Anr reported in 162 (2009) DLT 103 (DB) wherein recorded owner of the land was Gaon Sabha.

entities.text:
Raj Singh & Anr v. Union of India &
Anr reported in 162 (2009) DLT 103 (DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case Ld. ADJ had order 60% compensation to the occupant and 40% to Gaon Sabha.

In the said case of Raj Singh & Anr v. Union of India & Anr, the Hon'ble High Court had observed as under:
10.Different rights flow in favour of Bhumidhar and Asami, which are stipulated in the provisions of the Act contained from Sections 22 to 47 thereof.

entities.text: Raj Singh & Anr v. Union of India & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The position is summed up by the Division Bench in the case of Fateh Singh (supra) in the following manner: "10. Suffice would it be to record that there is a difference in the right of a Bhumidhar and the right of an Asami.

Three essential attributes attach to the rights of a Bhumidhar;
being (1) permanency of tenure; (2) hereditary character of the tenure; and (3) transferability of the tenure.
As against that, an Asami gets a lesser right.
Permanency of an Asami relates to the term of the grant (patta).
It is a non transferable right.
The right is hereditary but only for the remainder of the period of the grant (patta) on the death of the Asami.

Reference may be made to Section 32 and Section 68 of the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 to ascertain the rights of an Asami."

5

entities.text: Union Of India vs Brigadier Sanjay Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is because of the difference in nature of rights that flow in favour of bhumidars and asamis that this Court has given 60% share in the case to an Asami and 75% to a Bhumidhar.
11.The question, therefore, is as to what was the status of the appellants at the time of acquisition of the land in question.
As per the appellants, they were in actual physical and cultivatory possession of the entire subject land till the date of its acquisition.

Though it is stated that they were in continuous cultivatory possession of land for more than three years and therefore, entitled to be declared as Bhumidhar under Section 85 of the Act, it is also admitted at the same time that no such proceedings under Section 85 were initiated for getting their rights declared as Bhumidhar.

The appellants have admitted that because of the acquisition of land by the Government they could not file formal petition for declaration of Bhumidari rights in their favour in respect of the subject land.
It is also not in dispute that in the revenue record Gaon Sabha had been shown as Bhumidhar.
12.The position which emerges from the aforesaid admitted facts is that there is no declaration of the appellants as Bhumidhar.
The Gaon Sabha remained the recorded owner and also shown as Bhumidhar in the revenue records.
On the other hand, the appellants could only show their cultivatory possession as on the date of acquisition of the land.
The documents produced by them relate to the years 198284.
As already pointed out above, notification under Section 4 in this case was issued on 27.1.1984.
Therefore, till January 1984, as per the evidence produced on record, they had been in possession for two years.
Thus, on the basis of evidence produced, it is difficult to conclude that the appellants had acquired Bhumidhari rights.
At the most they would be treated as having Asami rights in the land in question.
Moreover, concededly no application for declaration as Bhumidar was filed as according to the appellants themselves, land came to be acquired.

13.It is only on the declaration of a person as Bhumidhar that he gets the three essential rights,
namely, permanency of tenure, hereditary character of the tenure and transferability of tenure.
Before such a person is declared as Bhumidhar, in terms of Section 74(4) of the Act he is to prove his entitlement for being declared as Bhumidhar after leading evidence.
In such proceedings, Gaon Sabha has a right to lead the evidence to rebut the claim of such claimants.
Before that stage he remains an Asami to which position he is admitted by the Gaon Sabha when put in possession of land for the purpose of cultivation.

The tenure of Asami is five years requiring land to be reclaimed within that period and reclamation proved as a condition for conferring Bhumidari right in the Asami with simultaneous extinguishment of Bhumidari right of the Gaon Sabha.
If Gaon Sabha succeeds in proving that the land was not reclaimed, the right of Asami lapses and possession reverts to the Gaon Sabha.
Therefore, these proceedings are of paramount importance and only on that basis the appellants could claim themselves to be Bhumidhar.
However, no such proceedings were even initiated in the instant case.
Thus, as per the record, the right of the appellants remained as that of Asami only.
In such a case, they would be entitled to 60% of the compensation.

13.5 Admittedly the fact of the matter is again that as per proceedings which were initiated U/s 81 of the DLR Act there is mention that a sum of Rs.2.5 lakh would cost for reconverting this land to agricultural land or usable for the purposes it was.
Gaon Sabha has not led any evidence to substantiate that it has incurred any expenses for making the land usable for cultivation or for the purposes as envisaged under the DLR Act.

Nothing much has been done qua the suit land after the vesting as in all probabilities the factual position at the ground remained as such that the Union Of India vs Brigadier Sanjay Sharma on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12267534/
6

sentences.text: construction activity was carried out  as manifested by the claim of IP VPS Dahiya and coupled with the fact that no amount was spent by Gaon Sabha towards restoration of the land.
Even the physical possession of the land was not taken by Gaon Sabha from the occupants.
13.6 As such in view of ratio of the case of Raj Singh (Supra), both the parties i.e. individual claimants and Gaon Sabha are entitled to the compensation at the ratio of 60% and 40%
respectively
vizaviz
the area of 201 sq yards and 200 sq yards i.e. qua Brigadier Sanjay Sharma and qua Lt Col. VPS Dahiya.
To my mind the same would be the most fair apportionment.

13.7 I may also note herein that aforesaid apportionment of compensation is concerned, Gaon Sabha's right to claim further/enhanced compensation more than 40% would have been there had it made the land usable for agricultural purposes which warrant taking physical possession of the same and making improvements thereon.

13.8 Worthwhile to mention here that if I look at Section 74 of the DLR Act 1954 the Gaon Sabha has a right to admit any person as Asami and objective of Section 74 is to make the land usable for cultivation purposes - which would again afford a ground to the so called Asami to seek declaration of rights as Bhumidar upon his establishing his continuous possession and complete reclaimation of land.
13.9

In this regard I also rely upon a judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of Gaon Sabha Kakrola v. Sarbati & Ors LA Appeal No.198/2007 decided by Hon'ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.

sentences.text: This was a case with respect to the disputes raised by the individual claimants who were allottees of land under 20 point programme and they had also subsequently initiated action U/s 74 (4) of the DLR Act for declaration as Bhumidars.

The discussion of the said case is as hereunder:
20.
On the issue at hand, we are guided and instructed by a decision of a coordinate bench of this Court reported as 117 (2005) DLT 588 (DB) Moti Lal Jain Vs. Mukhtiar Singh.

entities.text: 117 (2005) DLT 588 (DB) Moti Lal Jain Vs. Mukhtiar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. In Moti Lal Jain's case (supra) the Division Bench of this Court was considering the issue of apportionment between a Bhumidhar and a nonoccupancy tenant under the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887 whose claim for being declared an occupancy tenant was pending when the subject land of the said case was acquired.

22. The Division Bench held that the apportionment had to be in the ratio of 40% :
60% between the owner and the non occupancy tenant claiming right to be declared as an occupancy tenant.
Xxxx 26.

We dispose of the appeals modifying the apportionment effected vide impugned orders dated 15.11.2006 in LAC No.13/02, LAC No.14/02 and LAC No.17/02 by directing that the compensation determined on acquisition of the subject land would be apportioned in the ratio 40% : 60% in favour Union Of India vs Brigadier Sanjay Sharma on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12267534/
7 of the Gaon Sabha and the respondent(s) No.1 respectively in each case.

sentences.text: Relief.
14. In view of above, IP Gaon Sabha Village Tajpur Khurd is held entitled to 40% of the compensation amount.
Further IP No.1 Brigadier Sanjay Sharma and IP No.2 Lt. Col. VPS Dahiya are held entitled to the share in compensation to the extent of 60% with respect of 201 and 200 sq yards.
Remaining amount be kept in FDR.
Reference petition stands accordingly answered.
A copy of this award be sent to the Land Acquisition Collected for his information.
File be consigned to record room.
